title: ANA 201 : AXILLARY VEIN AND LYMPH NODES
subject: ANA 201

questions.question: The axillary vein is formed at the lower border of which muscle?
questions.explanation: The text states the axillary vein is formed at the lower border of the teres major muscle.

questions.question: Which two veins unite to form the axillary vein?
options: Basilic vein and venae comitantes of the brachial artery
Internal jugular vein and subclavian vein
questions.explanation: The axillary vein is formed by the union of the basilic vein and venae comitantes of the brachial artery.

questions.question: Along which side of the axillary artery does the axillary vein run?
questions.explanation: The axillary vein runs upwards along the medial side of the axillary artery.

questions.question: The axillary vein ends at the outer border of the first rib by becoming which vein?
questions.explanation: It ends at the outer border of the first rib by becoming the subclavian vein.

questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the axillary vein?
questions.explanation: The veins corresponding to the branches of the axillary artery, namely the lateral thoracic vein and subscapular vein, are tributaries.

questions.question: The cephalic vein joins the axillary vein after piercing which fascia?
questions.explanation: The text states the cephalic vein joins it after piercing the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question: Why can the axillary vein freely expand during increased venous return?
options: There is no or very thin axillary sheath around it
questions.explanation: The text notes there is no or a very thin axillary sheath around the vein, allowing it to expand freely.

questions.question: The spontaneous thrombosis of the axillary vein can be caused by compression from which structure?
questions.explanation: A muscular band called the axillary arch may compress the vein, causing spontaneous thrombosis.

questions.question: How many axillary lymph nodes are typically present in the axilla?
questions.explanation: The text states their number varies between 20 and 30.

questions.question: The axillary lymph nodes are divided into how many groups?
questions.explanation: They are divided into five groups: anterior, posterior, lateral, central, and apical.

questions.question: Which group of lymph nodes lies along the lateral thoracic vein at the lower border of the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The anterior or pectoral group lies along the lateral thoracic vein at the lower border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: The axillary tail of Spence is in direct contact with which lymph node group?
questions.explanation: The text states the axillary tail of Spence is in actual contact with the anterior lymph nodes.

questions.question: Which group of lymph nodes lies on the posterior axillary fold along the subscapular vein?
questions.explanation: The posterior or subscapular group lies on the posterior axillary fold along the subscapular vein.

questions.question: Which group of lymph nodes drains lymph from the upper limb?
questions.explanation: The lateral group drains the lymph from the upper limb.

questions.question: Enlargement of the central group of lymph nodes may compress which nerve?
questions.explanation: The intercostobrachial nerve passes amongst these nodes; enlargement can compress it.

questions.question: Where are the apical or infraclavicular group of lymph nodes situated?
options: In the upper part of the axilla
questions.explanation: The apical or infraclavicular group is situated deep to the clavipectoral fascia at the apex of the axilla.

questions.question: On the right side, the apical lymph nodes drain into which structure?
questions.explanation: They drain into the subclavian lymph trunk on the right side.

questions.question: On the left side, the apical lymph nodes drain into which structure?
questions.explanation: On the left side, they drain into the thoracic duct.

questions.question: How can the deeply located apical lymph nodes be palpated?
options: By pushing fingers into the apex of the axilla from below
By pressing on the anterior chest wall
By palpating the posterior axillary fold
By palpating the lower border of pectoralis minor
questions.explanation: They can be palpated by pushing fingers into the apex of the axilla from below and behind the clavicle from above.

questions.question: Level I axillary lymph nodes lie in which relation to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: Level I nodes lie lateral to the lower border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: Level II axillary lymph nodes lie in which relation to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: Level II nodes lie deep to the pectoralis minor muscle.

questions.question: Level III axillary lymph nodes lie in which relation to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: Level III nodes lie medial to the upper border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: What is the term for the first lymph nodes to receive lymph from a breast area involved in cancer?
questions.explanation: These are termed sentinel lymph nodes.

questions.question: Sentinel lymph nodes are usually which level of lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: The text states sentinel nodes are usually the level I lymph nodes.

questions.question: How are sentinel lymph nodes confirmed clinically?
questions.explanation: They are confirmed by injecting a radioactive substance into the affected area of the breast.

questions.question: What is the primary reason axillary lymph nodes are palpated during a clinical examination?
options: To check for infection in the arm
Due to their involvement in breast cancer
questions.explanation: Palpation is part of the clinical examination of the breast due to their involvement in cancer.

questions.question: An axillary abscess arises from infection of which structure?
questions.explanation: The abscess arises from infection and suppuration of the axillary lymph nodes.

questions.question: The pus of an axillary abscess may track into the arm if it enters which structure?
questions.explanation: The pus may track into the neck or arm if it enters the axillary sheath.

questions.question: Where is the incision made to drain an axillary abscess?
options: In the apex of the axilla
In the floor of the axilla
questions.explanation: The abscess is drained by giving an incision in the floor of the axilla.

questions.question: Why is the incision for an axillary abscess made nearer to the medial wall?
options: To access the lymph nodes easily
To avoid injury to the main vessels
questions.explanation: The incision is made nearer the medial wall to avoid injury to the main vessels running along the walls of the axilla.
